title: [finding] plugin-chatbot's SDUI renderer casts `messages as any` across the @object-ui/types ↔ plugin-chatbot `ChatMessage` boundary
body:
Found while implementing #4383 (converging plugin-chatbot's two `ChatMessage` types). Out of that card's scope — it is a **cross-package** seam, not the barrel collision #4383 owns — so filing it rather than fixing it. Unassigned, `finding`-labelled, no `pm:queue`: nothing a user hits today (evidence below).

## Fact

After #4383, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` exports one `ChatMessage`. `@object-ui/types` **also** exports a `ChatMessage`, and it is a different shape. Both are deliberate — one is the JSON/SDUI authoring contract, the other the React runtime contract — but they meet inside one file, and the meeting point is three `as any` casts:

- `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/renderer.tsx:77` (`chatbot`)
- `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/renderer.tsx:285` (`chatbot-enhanced`)
- `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/renderer.tsx:414` (`chatbot-floating`)

`renderer.tsx` imports `ChatMessage` from `@object-ui/types`, feeds `schema.messages` through `useObjectChat`, and hands the result to components whose `messages` prop is the plugin's own `ChatMessage`. The cast is what makes that compile.

Three declared drifts between the two:

| key | `@object-ui/types` (authoring) | `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` (runtime) |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | `'user' \| 'assistant' \| 'system' \| 'tool'` | `'user' \| 'assistant' \| 'system'` |
| `timestamp` | `string \| Date` | `string` |
| `metadata` | `Record` (via `z.record`) | not declared |

`'tool'` and `Date` are genuinely authorable: `ChatMessageSchema` in `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts:229` declares `z.enum([… 'tool'])` and `z.union([z.string(), z.date()])`.

## Why `finding` and not a defect

Both drifts are absorbed at the runtime seam, so no user-visible failure exists today — this is dormant type drift, not a bug:

- `timestamp`: `normalizeMessages` in `useObjectChat.ts:261` coerces `msg.timestamp instanceof Date ? msg.timestamp.toISOString() : …`, so a `Date` never reaches a React child. (Without that it would be the classic "Objects are not valid as a React child" throw when `showTimestamp` is on.)
- `role: 'tool'`: `formatMessageProps` at `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx:847` returns `role === 'user' ? 'user' : 'assistant'`, so a tool message renders as an assistant bubble. Content is shown, nothing is lost, nothing throws.

## Why it is still worth a card

The `as any` is the only thing holding the two contracts apart, and it erases **all** of the drift rather than the parts that are intentional. If either vocabulary moves — a new schema `role`, a required runtime key — the cast will keep compiling and the mismatch will surface as rendering behaviour instead of a type error. The honest shapes would be an explicit adapter at the seam (schema message to runtime message, one function, its narrowing decisions written down and tested), which also gives `role: 'tool'` a named rendering decision instead of an implicit fallthrough.

## Anchor

Measured on `claude/issue-4383-chatmessage-collision` at `14613a863` (branch point `bb58d1d61`, 2026-08-12). Reproduce: `git grep -n "messages as any" -- packages/plugin-chatbot/src/renderer.tsx`.

Related: #4383 (the in-package collision, fixed), #4040.
